sentences.text:
Shri Ravinandan Dwivedi - Advocate for appellant No.1.
 Shri Krishna Kumar Verma - Advocate for appellant No.2.

Shri Yash Soni - Deputy Advocate General for the respon Heard on I.A. No.2873/2023, fourth application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant No.1- Pappu.
His first application was already dismissed on merits vide order dated 17.11.2017.
2. Also heard on I.A. No.18740/2024, fourth application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant No.2 Ramveer.

His first application was already dismissed on merits vide order dated 21.02.2017.
3.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 15.07.2015 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Bijawar, District Chhatarpur (M.P.) in S.T. No.01/2013, whereby the each of the appellants have been convicted and sentenced as under:
Appellant No.1- Pappu Conviction U/s. Imprisonment Fine In lieu of default 363 of IPC R.I. for 3 years Rs.2000/- Additional R.I. for 3 months 366 of IPC R.I. for 5 years Rs.3000/- Additional R.I. for 5 months 376(2)(g) of IPC Life imprisonment Rs.5000/- Additional R.I. for 1 year 2 CRA-1930-2015 Appellant No.2- Ramveer Conviction U/s. Imprisonment Fine In lieu of default 376(2)(g) of IPC Life imprisonment Rs.5000/- Additional R.I. for 1 year 4.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellants.

As per prosecution, the allegation against the appellants is that they kidnapped the prosecutrix from the lawful guardianship of her parents and took her in the forest and and committed sexual intercourse with the her without her consent on the pretext of marriage.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the prosecutrix was aged about 17 years at the time of incident.
Learned counsel further submits that there seems to be a consensual relationship between the prosecutrix and the appellants.
Learned counsel also submits that the age of the prosecutrix was not proved.
There is no eye witness in the case.
The prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt therefore, benefit of doubt ought to have been given to the appellants.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses.

The appellants have already undergone about 10 years of incarceration, therefore, in the light of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh Vs. The State of Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161720287/
1 Uttar Pradesh [SLP (Cri.) No.4633/2021], the application may be considered on the ground of period of incarceration.

sentences.text: This appeal is of the year 2015 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
They are ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7 . Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Saudan Singh (supra) as well as the period of incarceration already undergone by the appellants, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellants can be considered.

8. Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I.A. No.2873/2023 and I.A.
No.18740/2024 are allowed.

9 . It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of both the appellants- Preetam and Ramveer is hereby suspended and they be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with one solvent surety of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 16.12.2025 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
10. List the matter for final hearing in due course.

(VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (AJAY KUMAR   JUDGE JUDG  Shanu Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161720287/
